title: Hill Climbing
html:
When only the final state matters — not the path — local search keeps one current state and repeatedly moves to a better neighbour. It uses almost no memory and handles huge or continuous spaces, but it can get stuck.

Local search — an optimisation method that works on complete-state formulations (every state is a full candidate solution) and improves it by small changes. Used for n-queens, scheduling, circuit layout, travelling salesperson, and — in continuous form — training neural networks by gradient descent.

The objective function (or cost) defines a state-space landscape. Hill climbing moves uphill (maximising) or downhill (minimising cost) until no neighbour is better.

Steepest-ascent hill climbing on 8-queens

State: one queen per column, state[c] = its row. Neighbours: move one queen within its column (8 × 7 = 56 neighbours). Cost h: pairs of queens attacking each other.

Why it gets stuck

Local maximum

A peak higher than every neighbour but lower than the global maximum. Every move looks worse, so the search stops.

Plateau / shoulder

A flat region: all neighbours have the same value. No gradient to follow — the search wanders or stops.

Ridge

A sequence of local maxima that rises diagonally; single moves in any axis go down, so progress is very slow.

Variants that escape

VariantIdeaEffect on 8-queens (textbook figures)
Steepest ascentTake the best neighbourSolves ~14% of starts, in ~4 steps
Sideways movesAllow up to k moves to equal-valued neighbours (plateaus)~94% solved, ~21 steps
Stochastic hill climbingPick randomly among uphill moves, weighted by steepnessSlower but finds better peaks on some landscapes
First-choiceGenerate random neighbours until one is betterGood when there are thousands of neighbours
Random-restartRun from random starts until a solution appearsComplete with probability → 1; expected restarts ≈ 1/p
Key point

Random-restart hill climbing is surprisingly strong: with success probability p per run, it needs 1/p runs on average. For 8-queens, p ≈ 0.14 gives ~7 runs; with sideways moves, millions of queens can be solved in seconds.

Watch out

Hill climbing is incomplete — it can stop at a local optimum and report it as the answer. Always ask: what is the landscape like, and how will the search escape a local optimum?

What is the main weakness of hill climbing and how do you fix it?

It gets stuck on local maxima, plateaus and ridges because it only accepts improvements. Fixes: random restarts, sideways moves, stochastic moves, or accepting some downhill moves (simulated annealing).

How is gradient descent related to hill climbing?

Gradient descent is hill climbing (descending) in a continuous space: the neighbour is chosen by stepping along the negative gradient. It has the same local-minimum issue, softened in deep learning by noise (SGD), momentum and the high-dimensional landscape.
